title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and canonical runbooks. It is intended as the single-source reference for teams that operate customer-facing inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane). The guidance below is production-facing: measurable, actionable, and tied to ownership.

Scope

- Services covered: api-gateway, inference-runtime, kv-cache-service, batching-service, model-router, telemetry-pipeline, auth-service.
- Audience: SRE, on-call engineers, service owners, release engineers, product managers.
- Not covered: experimental research infra, personal dev sandboxes.

SLOs and Error Budgets

Summary of primary SLOs (applies to public hosted API and Dedicated control plane endpoints):

1) Availability SLOs (per-route)
- SLO id: SLO-AV-001
- Description: Successful request ratio (HTTP 2xx + 3xx) for /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints
- Target: 99.95% rolling 30d
- Measurement: Datadog metric inference.request.success_count / inference.request.total_count, evaluated in 1m buckets, aggregated to 30d rolling window
- Error budget: 0.05% of requests (30d)

2) P99 Latency SLO (tail latency)
- SLO id: SLO-LT-001
- Description: P99 server-side latency for text generation endpoints (end-to-end server processing, excludes network egress)
- Target: 450ms for small/fast models; 1200ms for large models (e.g., 70B FP16)
- Measurement: tracing span inference.request.processing_latency_ms; compute P99 per route daily and maintain 30d rolling compliance

3) Embeddings Throughput SLO
- SLO id: SLO-EMB-001
- Description: 95th percentile throughput for embeddings batch endpoints under steady-state traffic
- Target: >= 1,200 reqs/min per allocation for standard SKU, 99th percentile request success rate >= 99.9%

SLO Ownership and Tiering

- Each SLO has a documented owner (on-call rotation service owner) and a backup owner. Owners must be listed on the service README and in the oncall roster.
- Tiering: Critical (API production routes), Important (internal admin routes), Development (non-prod). Only Critical SLOs have error budgets that trigger org-level actions.

Error Budget Burn and Remedies

- Burn calculation: daily burn = (target - observed) / target across 30d window expressed as percent of budget used.
- Triggers and actions:
  - Burn > 10% over 7d: service owner notification and postmortem if root cause unknown.
  - Burn > 25% over 7d: pause non-essential feature releases; require dedicated mitigation run (see \"Mitigation Playbook\").
  - Burn > 50% in 30d: Escalate to SRE leadership; initiate org-level rollback and traffic-throttle plan.

Mitigation Playbook (high level)

1) Immediately confirm measurement validity (aggregation windows, instrumentation regression). Check telemetry-pipeline and Datadog dashboards.
2) If measurements are valid, triage by symptom: increased latency, error class shift (5xx types), capacity saturation, external dependency failure (e.g., KMS, cloud storage).
3) Short-term mitigations (within 30-120 minutes): scale up inference-pool (manual or autoscaler override), enable degraded fast-model variant via model-router fallback, reduce batch size to lower tail latency, enable circuit-breakers for non-critical downstreams.
4) Medium-term (same day): schedule canary rollback, remove problematic feature flag, increase cache TTLs for prefix cache.
5) Long-term: implement root cause fixes, update runbooks, add improved dashboards/alerts.

Capacity Planning Process

Objective: ensure sufficient reserved capacity across Dedicated and Hosted fleets to meet demand while minimizing cost.

Quarterly capacity planning cadence:
1) Inputs: recent 90d traffic patterns, model mix (counts of small/medium/large variants), new customer onboarding pipeline (sales forecast), scheduled promos/benchmarks, historical growth curves.
2) Modeling: use the capacity-planner tool (CLI: tools/capacity-planner --input <traffic.csv> --profile <sku>) to simulate required GPU-hours and expected unit latency with representative workloads.
3) Headroom targets: Target 20% buffer on expected p99 load for critical routes; 40% for large-model pools with known variability.
4) Purchasing and reservations: Finance + Eng Infra to negotiate reserved capacity 60d in advance for Dedicated customers.
5) Validation: Run stress tests and synthetic traffic via bench/traffic-generator to verify p99 latency and throughput. Mark green/red in capacity board.

Operational runbooks for capacity incidents:

- Runbook: capacity-surge
  - Symptoms: p95/p99 latency increases with GPU utilization > 85% sustained for 10m, queue growth in batching-service, OOM events in runtime logs.
  - Immediate steps:
    1) Check autoscaler status: k get hpa --namespace serving (or use internal autoscaler UI).
    2) If autoscaling stalled, manually scale pool: tools/pool-scale --pool <pool-id> --replicas +2 (estimate).
    3) Throttle new requests: update rate-limit policy for non-priority tenants via admin-console (route: /admin/ratelimit).
    4) If scaling cannot keep up, enable fast-model fallback for best-effort customers and apply quota enforcement.
  - Post-incident: run capacity retrospective and update forecasts in capacity-planner.

Reliability Initiatives and Prioritization

- Initiative examples (current roadmap):
  - Reduce KV cache miss rates by 30% through smarter prefix replication (owner: infra/cache team, Q2).
  - Improve p99 tail latency by 20% via batching-service backpressure improvements and RPC timeouts tuning (owner: serving-runtime, Q1).
  - End-to-end canary automation for model rollouts so misbehaving models auto-rollback on quality/regression signals (owner: applied-ml-and-evals, multi-team).

Prioritization framework:
- Criteria: customer impact (SLOs affected), probability of recurrence, engineering effort, cost savings. Use RICE scoring for quarter planning and SRE leadership will triage top 6 initiatives each quarter.

Incident Review Standards (Postmortems)

- For any outage that consumes >= 25% of an SLO error budget in 7d, or causes customer-visible downtime > 5m, an incident review is required.
- Template (required sections):
  1) Summary (one paragraph)
  2) Impact (SLOs, customers affected, duration)
  3) Timeline (high-resolution events)
  4) Root cause analysis (technical and organizational factors)
  5) Corrective actions (immediate and long-term), owners, and ETA
  6) Verification plan and success metrics
  7) Lessons learned and follow-up tasks
- Reviewer cadence: draft within 72 hours, review with stakeholders within 7 days, publish within 14 days.

Operational Tooling and Dashboards

Canonical dashboards and alerts (examples):
- dashboard: SRE / Inference - SLO Overview (shows per-route availability, latency percentiles, error budget burn rate)
- dashboard: Serving - Pool Health (GPU utilization, queue length, per-host OOMs)
- alert: SLO_BURN_WARNING (error_budget_burn_rate > 0.1 for 7d) -> notify #sre-slos and owner
- alert: POOL_HIGH_UTIL (gpu_utilization > 85% for 10m) -> page on-call and post to #sre-ops
- alert: P99_LATENCY_SPIKE (p99 > threshold for route sustained 5m) -> fire to on-call with runbook link

Tooling inventory and responsibilities:
- capacity-planner (cli, owned by eng-sre) - modeling and reservation planner
- bench/traffic-generator (bench team) - reproducible load tests and canaries
- telemetry-pipeline (owned by eng-platform) - ingestion, prom->datadog bridge, sampling rules
- oncall-dashboard (internal UI) - quick actions: scale pool, flip fallback, set rate limits

Runbook Templates and Examples

- Runbook: inference-5xx-spike
  - Purpose: triage and mitigate a sudden increase in 5xx errors from inference-runtime
  - Pager routing: Primary on-call for inference-runtime -> escalation to senior SRE after 15m
  - Steps:
    1) Gather context: timestamp, routes affected, recent deploys, customer commits. Query: tools/query-logs --service inference-runtime --since 15m --filter status>=500
    2) Check runtime metrics: out-of-memory, GPU kernel errors, queue backpressure, thread pool saturation.
    3) If OOM: increase allowed memory or roll back recent model changes, restart affected hosts behind load balancer (command: scripts/restart-host --host <id>).
    4) If external dependency failing (e.g., KMS): switch to cached keys for short TTL and notify security (owner: security-and-compliance).
    5) Communicate: update incident channel with status and ETA every 15 minutes.
    6) If mitigation succeeds, schedule postmortem and permanent fix.

On-call Responsibilities and Routines

- Handoff checklist: summarize ongoing incidents, outstanding action items, and any planned maintenance. Handoffs must be documented in oncall-dashboard.
- Daily routine: check SLO dashboard at start of shift, verify no rapid burn, review queued alerts, and confirm backups/snapshots ran overnight.
- Incident comms: use standardized incident topic prefix: [INC][service-name][severity]. Publish a public customer-facing status blurb for incidents impacting Hosted API.

Metrics, Logging and Tracing Standards

- Metrics: tag all SLO-related metrics with service, route, model_variant, region, and tenant_id where possible. Use cardinality controls for tenant tags.
- Tracing: include request_id and model_version in root span. Ensure sampling keeps at least 1% of requests with full traces and higher for anomalous errors.
- Logs: structured JSON, include severity, request_id, host_id, GPU_id, error_type. Retention policy: 60 days hot, archive 12 months.

Compliance and Audit Steps

- Quarterly audit of SLO measurements (owner: eng-sre) to validate instrumentation parity with expected definitions.
- Maintain a public SLO board for stakeholders showing current burn and forecast.

Appendices

A) Example Datadog Query (Availability SLO)
- numerator: sum:inference.request.success_count{route:*/v1/generate}.as_count()
- denominator: sum:inference.request.total_count{route:*/v1/generate}.as_count()
- availability: 100 * numerator / denominator

B) Useful CLI commands
- Check pool status: tools/pool-status --pool inference-production --format json
- Manually scale: tools/pool-scale --pool inference-production --replicas +2 --reason "emergency-scale"
- Query recent logs: tools/query-logs --service inference-runtime --since 30m --filter "level>=error" --limit 200

C) Contact matrix
- SRE on-call: paged via PagerDuty -> primary: inference-runtime-oncall
- Eng infra emergencies: infra-oncall@redwood.com
- Product security contacts: security@redwood.com

D) Change history
- 2026-02-15: Document created (Ari Chen)
- 2026-03-01: Clarified burn thresholds and added capacity runbook steps (Maya Patel)

If you are an owner for a service not listed here, add your SLO definitions and runbooks following the templates above and request a review from eng-sre. For questions about applying these standards to Dedicated or Private deployments, contact eng-sre@redwood.com.
